title: Freetown Colony
capsule: The Province of Freedom was established in 1787 when the abolitionist-backed St George's Bay Company settled approximately 400 Black Poor and formerly enslaved people from London on land purchased from the Koya Temne chieftain Naimbanna at the Sierra Leone estuary. Disease and conflict devastated the initial settlement, and King Jimmy of the Temne burned it in 1789; the surviving settlers were reorganized when the Sierra Leone Company refounded the colony as Freetown in 1792. The short-lived 1787–1797 Province of Freedom represents the first organized British attempt to create a self-governing community of freed Africans and Black Loyalists on the West African coast.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The settlement's existence and approximate coastal location are well documented in British parliamentary and company records; its precise territorial claims over hinterland areas are essentially nil for this period.
